plain: Cannot be canceled or made void

webster.text: Not to be defeated; that cannot be made void; as an indefeasible estate or title.

example.quote: That the people have an indubitable, unalienable, and indefeasible right to reform or change their government, whenever it be found adverse or inadequate to the purposes of its institution.
example.cite: James Madison, Speeches in Congress, June 1789, as transcribed at constitution.org (the page is dated June 8, 1789; the House removal debate ran June 16-22, 1789, and his amendments were offered June 8)
